why: Dev 2020-22 at openers: market-only soft-vs-sharp gaps had ~zero CLV (ml_any_sharp2 n=48, CLV[all] +0.04%; dog/spread variants negative), vs +2-5% for the same rules at later snapshots. ml_any_sharp2 is frozen anyway as the DIRECT test of 'are openers exploitable by soft-vs-sharp shopping' (expected to fail). ml_model5_clean (model win prob >= market+5pp and model EV >= 3%, only games with no QB on any report/no QB change and both teams' previous games final at the snapshot) was the best less-contaminated model rule at the opener (n=86, CLV[all] +1.98%, p=0.043; later snapshots +0.73%). Caveat: p_model still uses final-report non-QB injury inputs (look-ahead), so a pass would be an upper bound.
bet_placement: opener snapshots only (Sun 23:30 and Mon 04:00 UTC, games 72-216h away); one bet per game at the first qualifying opener snapshot, best-scoring book/side; books = my_books.json present in the region-us opener file; sanity filters as edge_lab._prep
pass_bar: mean price-based CLV (ML: p_close_all; spread: mu_close_all via key-number pricing) > 0 with one-sided p < 0.025 (0.05/2)
